messages:
laura: Heads up — I found a staging .env accidentally committed in frontend repo. Looks like REDIS_URL (plaintext) and a GCP service account key are in frontend/.env.staging. Commit: abc123. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/frontend/commit/abc123

sam: :eyes: can you paste the file path and confirm whether CI published any artifacts that could include it? pinging @ops-oncall

laura: path is frontend/.env.staging (commit abc123). CI log for the publish job shows the package bundle step ran and uploaded tgz to our internal npm registry. I did `git show abc123:frontend/.env.staging` and confirmed the SA key snippet is there. Not production creds but treat as compromised.

mike: If there's a GCP SA key present we should revoke it immediately. Steps: revoke SA key via gcloud, rotate any KMS wrapping key if it was used to encrypt the keyfile, and rotate Redis password. Also check Vault access patterns for that path.

anya: I'll take SA + Redis rotation. Plan: 1) Revoke SA key in GCP: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <key-id> --iam-account=sa-frontend@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com` 2) Create new SA key with least privilege 3) Update Vault secret at `secret/data/teams/frontend/staging` with new values 4) Restart Vault-agent sidecars for canary.

sam: Before rotation, capture audit evidence. I scanned vault-audit and saw several reads of `secret/data/teams/frontend/staging` from IP 10.8.9.22 (ci-runner) between 2026-03-15T14:11:00Z and 2026-03-15T14:19:00Z. We need to assume exfiltration to internal registry is possible. Also run `npm view`/registry search for that package version.

vault-bot: Audit snippet: 2026-03-15T14:12:32Z vault audit: request_id=7f3b... principal=ci-runner policy=ci-runner-policy path=secret/data/teams/frontend/staging op=read status=200

ops-oncall: I'll isolate the runner and disable the publish. Taking npm package 2.3.1 offline from internal registry now. Also removing the runner's service account binding so it can't pull new tokens.

mike: We should tighten RBAC to avoid direct kv gets from CI. Proposal: 1) require AppRole for apps to fetch `secret/data/teams/*` 2) revoke create/list/delete for CI token scopes 3) enforce response_wrapping for any export of raw keys. I drafted a policy PR (link in repo).

laura: Timeline proposal: rotate creds and update Vault by EOD PST. Who owns what: @anya rotates GCP SA + Redis, @mike applies Vault policy changes and updates the secret, @ops-oncall takes registry actions, @sam collects audit evidence and notifies incident channel/legal if needed. I'll drive the comms.

sam: Checklist I'm tracking: 1) Revoke GCP SA keys 2) Rotate Redis password (rolling restart) 3) Update Vault secret at `secret/data/teams/frontend/staging` and add metadata `rotated_by:laura` 4) Revoke CI tokens and issue short-lived tokens via OIDC/STS 5) Search artifact storage & s3 for exposed key 6) Apply RBAC policy changes and enable stricter audit logging for KMS usage.

laura: I pushed a draft PR for the RBAC changes to `infra/vault/policies/frontend-staging.hcl` — uses AppRole and denies direct `delete` for non-admins. Please review: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/789

anya: After rotation I'll run canary smoke tests. Plan: update vault secret, deploy canary to 5% traffic, validate connection to Redis and GCS with new SA, then ramp. Will post smoke outputs here.

mike: Quick KMS note: check if SA keyfile was wrapped with GCP KMS. If so, list key versions: `gcloud kms keys versions list --key=projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...` and rewrap with a new key version or create a new key and re-encrypt secrets. If KMS key material is suspect, rotate following GCP rewrap procedure.

sam: Do we need an emergency Vault master rewrap? Not yet. No evidence that our master encryption key left the cluster. Only the service account keyfile appears to be in the commit. If we find the SA in a public gist or external registry, escalate to full incident.

ops-oncall: Registry taken offline for that package version. Legal has been notified. Posting a short incident summary to #incidents and tagging security leads.

laura: Starting rotations now. I'll update progress here. :thumbsup:

laura: Update 14:40 PST — GCP SA key revoked, new key created and stored in Vault. Redis password rotated and updated in Vault. Updated `secret/data/teams/frontend/staging` with new values and `rotated_by:laura`. Apps are on a 5% canary deploy.

anya: Canary passed basic smoke, apps are fetching secrets via Vault agent successfully. I'll increase to 25% in 15m then full after 30m.

mike: I applied the temporary RBAC tightening for staging and scheduled a safer policy rollout for prod tomorrow. Also enabled extra audit logging on Vault and KMS for the next 7 days.

sam: Collected audit bundle and uploaded to secure vault zip at gs://internal-sec-audit/archives/1788888888.zip. Confirmed no external public references found in quick scan.

ops-oncall: Incident update posted. No customer impact. Marking incident as security-low for now, will keep monitoring.

laura: Thanks everyone for quick responses. We'll keep the postmortem notes minimal but include detection gap: npm publish step packaged .env; action item to add pre-publish gitignore enforcement and CI lint to fail on .env presence.

mike: Agreed — adding `prevent-env-in-tgz` lint rule and a registry blocker for packages containing sensitive file patterns.

laura: Closing loop: all rotations done, RBAC changes staged, extra audit enabled. I'll open a short postmortem tomorrow with timeline and detection/playbook updates. :white_check_mark:
